Article Title: Rain could play spoilsport as India’s dominance faces weather hurdle on Day 3 in Galle
Article Text:
Rain likely to play spoilsport on Day 3 in Galle (Image: TOI/Sahil Malhotra)

India in command after Padikkal's masterclass

Day 3 of the first Test between India and Sri Lanka in Galle is under a significant rain threat, with an 83% overall chance of precipitation forecast for the day. After rain disrupted proceedings on Day 2, another stop-start day could be on the cards.India remain firmly in control after reaching 460/9 at stumps on Day 2, with Devdutt Padikkal's magnificent 167 providing the foundation for a huge first-innings total. The visitors will now look to add a few more runs before turning their attention to Sri Lanka's batting line-up.As per AccuWeather forecast offers little encouragement for uninterrupted play, with rain chances remaining significant across all three sessions. The morning session is expected to begin with a 51% chance of rain at 10am, easing slightly to around 47% at 11am. The threat remains persistent around midday, with precipitation chances at 44% at noon and 48% at 1pm.The rain risk is expected to peak at around 52% at 2pm, before easing marginally during the final session. The probability stands at 45% at 3pm and could drop to 34% by 5pm.With the weather remaining unpredictable, ground staff could once again face a busy day at the Galle International Stadium.India will resume from 460/9, having dominated large portions of the opening two days. The standout performer has been Devdutt Padikkal, who produced a superb 167 to anchor India's innings and underline his growing credentials at No. 3. His innings proved particularly valuable as India continued to pile on the runs despite interruptions.With only one wicket remaining, India will be keen to stretch their advantage further before handing Sri Lanka the opportunity to bat. The hosts, meanwhile, face the daunting prospect of taking on an Indian bowling attack with a huge first-innings total already on the board.
Article Summary: India remain firmly in control after reaching 460/9 at stumps on Day 2. Devdutt Padikkal's magnificent 167 provided the foundation for a huge first-innings total. The visitors will now look to add a few more runs before turning their attention to Sri Lanka's batting line-up.

Article Title: 17 years on, from Hyderabad to New Delhi: How India became a badminton powerhouse
Article Text:
Satwiksairaj Rankireddy, Chirag Shetty, and PV Sindhu

From a host to a major badminton market

From Padukone to Sindhu, Satwik-Chirag

A very different India from Hyderabad 2009

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi represents the next chapter

When the world’s best badminton players walk into the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium on Monday, India will not merely be hosting the World Championships for the second time. Seventeen years after Hyderabad staged the event, the tournament returns to a country where badminton has grown multiple folds — in popularity, participation, elite success and commercial reach.The transformation is visible in the numbers. Forty-three per cent of Indians follow badminton, while 32% actively participate in the sport, making it the country's second-most played sport and its leading racket sport. At the Paris Olympics, badminton was the most-followed sport among Indian consumers, with 21% saying they would follow it, according to a YouGov poll.In 2009, India was already a passionate badminton nation, but the sport's footprint today is on an entirely different scale.India now hosts four BWF World Tour tournaments every year, underlining its importance on the international calendar. The India Open alone reached a potential 403 million household viewers across broadcast and digital platforms in 2024.That commercial growth has been accompanied by a much deeper Indian presence at the highest level.India's first World Championships medal came through Prakash Padukone in 1983.Since 2011, however, an Indian player or pair has won a medal at every edition, creating a remarkable 15-year streak of podium finishes.The list of medallists also shows how India's strength has expanded across generations and disciplines.Saina Nehwal won silver in 2015 and bronze in 2017, while PV Sindhu became India's biggest World Championships star, winning five medals, including the country's first and only gold in 2019.Kidambi Srikanth won silver and Lakshya Sen bronze in 2021, HS Prannoy added another men's singles bronze in 2023, while Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty have established India as a force in men's doubles with medals in 2022 and 2025.The three Olympic medals won by Indian badminton players — Saina's bronze at London 2012 and Sindhu's silver at Rio 2016 and bronze at Tokyo 2020 — further underline the country's rise.And perhaps the biggest sign of the sport's expanding ecosystem is para-badminton.India now has more than 1,000 athletes in national training programmes and 302 internationally classified players, while Indian para-badminton athletes have won more than 1,200 international medals in the past decade. The country has also collected nine Paralympic badminton medals, including golds at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024.The contrast with the last World Championships in India is striking.Hyderabad 2009 was dominated by China, which won four of the five gold medals. Three of the five finals featured players or pairs from the same country, reflecting the concentration of power that characterised the sport at the time.The badminton world has since become considerably more competitive — and India has been an important part of that transformation.Countries such as Japan, Chinese Taipei, Thailand and India have established themselves as regular contenders, while France, Canada and Singapore have also produced major breakthroughs. World champions have emerged from nations that once had little presence at the very top, including Thailand, Spain, Singapore and Malaysia.India, meanwhile, has gone from being represented by individual stars to becoming a multi-discipline medal contender.That makes the return of the World Championships to India more than a 17-year homecoming. It is a reflection of how far the sport has travelled in the country since Hyderabad.The numbers tell the story: a massive participation base, a huge fan following, four annual World Tour events, a rapidly expanding commercial footprint and an Indian medal at every World Championships since 2011.There is also a new generation ready to carry that legacy forward.If Hyderabad 2009 showcased India as an enthusiastic host watching the world's best, New Delhi 2026 arrives with India firmly established as one of badminton's major global markets and competitive forces.Seventeen years ago, India hosted the World Championships. This time, it hosts them as a badminton powerhouse — and with the opportunity to add another chapter to a remarkable rise.
Article Summary: The World Championships returns to India for the second time in 17 years. Hyderabad hosted the event in 2009, but India is now a major badminton market. Badminton is the country's second-most played sport and its leading racket sport. The India Open alone reached a potential 403 million household viewers in 2024.

Article Title: The ninety minutes! Moving day comes early in gloomy Galle
Article Text:
Sri Lanka's captain Dhananjaya de Silva takes a catch to dismiss India's Dhruv Jurel during the second day of the first Test cricket match between Sri Lanka and India in Galle, Sri Lanka, Sunday, Aug. 16, 2026. (AP Photo/Eranga Jayawardena)

TimesofIndia.com in Galle:

Galle: India's Dhruv Jurel celebrates his half century on day two of the first Test cricket match between India and Sri Lanka, in Galle, Sri Lanka. (PTI Photo/Shailendra Bhojak) (PTI08_16_2026_000284B)

Galle, Aug 16 (IANS) Relentless and stop-start rain since Sunday morning has finally relented to pave the way for play to commence on day two of the first Test between India and Sri Lanka, with action now set to commence at 2:35pm at the Galle International Stadium here on Sunday.

Brief Scores

India 1st innings:

The build-up to the second day of the Test focused on how many runs India needed before making Sri Lanka bat. Bat once and bat big had been the undertone of this fixture, and India's solid start on the opening day pointed in that direction. However, just like the weather, the mood changed at a frantic pace when Sri Lanka took the second new ball to dent India's hopes of batting the hosts out of the contest.Three overnight batters, Rishabh Pant, KL Rahul (who retired hurt on Day 1) and centurion Devdutt Padikkal, were dismissed in the first ninety minutes of play after the weather kept both camps confined to the dressing room for over five hours. From 'how much is too much' to 'how long will they survive', the nature of the conversations changed after a period in which the Sri Lanka bowlers sustained pressure.Debutant Keshara Nuwantha was the wrecker-in-chief, and his adjustment of length proved ideal for the Day 2 surface, which offered sharp turn and encouraging bounce. Day 3 is widely considered the moving day in a multi-day fixture, but it came earlier than usual as Pant couldn't convert his start, Rahul was undone by sharp turn and an even better catch, and Jadeja was trapped in front by a delivery that went on with the arm from the perfect length.Amid all the first-session chaos, the most assured batter from the visitors' camp held fort for a while, continuing from where he had left off, and looked set for a double hundred before falling for 167. Left-arm spinner Prabath Jayasuriya took the prized wicket of Padikkal and later dismissed another set batter, Dhruv Jurel, who scored a breezy 51. Before being dismissed, Jurel looked very assured and added valuable runs with Manav Suthar, pushing India's total to a number that keeps them in a dominant position.The right-hander remained busy, and there was a sense of urgency in his stand with Suthar as they negotiated the Sri Lanka attack during the closing hour of play. They got together when Jadeja was dismissed in the 99th over, with the scoreboard reading 377/6, and added 55 runs for the seventh wicket. Gill, in the pre-match press conference, had stressed the contributions from the lower order, and the partnership between Jurel and Suthar was the kind of effort he was looking for to keep the momentum on their side.Galle was gloomy, the skies were angry, and the heavy downpour in the early hours meant the scheduled early start to make up for lost overs wasn't possible. To make matters worse, the constant hide-and-seek between clouds, sun and rain continued for over five hours, and even the groundstaff's best efforts were not enough as the rain refused to relent.They kept removing the covers after seeing clear skies, but all the hard work was undone as the strong crosswinds kept bringing the dark clouds over the stadium. The moment clear skies ahead offered hope, the darkness in the rearview forced the over-100-member team to keep panning and craning their necks in different directions. When the sun finally came out in all its glory, the synchronised effort took over, and within no time, the field was restored for Test cricket with the help of the two Super Soppers.The forecast for the next three days means interruptions of varying durations will continue, but India will hope they have scored enough runs to maintain momentum and give their bowlers a spring in their stride. The rain-interrupted day moved at a rapid pace, and with the pitch beginning to reveal the Galle flavour, we are in for a mouth-watering remaining three days, weather permitting!460 for 9 after 116 overs (Devdutt Padikkal 167, KL Rahul 82, Dhruv Jurel 51; Prabath Jayasuriya 4/109, Keshara Nuwantha 3/175)
Article Summary: Three overnight batters, Rishabh Pant, KL Rahul (who retired hurt on Day 1) and centurion Devdutt Padikkal, were dismissed in the first ninety minutes of play after the weather kept both camps confined to the dressing room for over five hours. India's Dhruv Jurel looked very assured and added valuable runs with Manav Suthar, pushing India's total to a number that keeps them in a dominant position.

Article Title: From 288/2 to 460/9: Sri Lanka spinners turn the tide on rain-hit Day 2
Article Text:
Devdutt Padikkal and Dhruv Jurel (Image: ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Finding their bite a tad late, Sri Lanka’s spinners finally showed up in the first Test against India at the Galle International Cricket Stadium, with the ‘King of Galle’, left-arm spinner Prabath Jayasuriya (4-109 in 39 overs), and debutant off-spinner Keshara Nuwantha (3-175 in 39 overs) sharing all seven wickets to fall.On a heavily rain-curtailed Day Two, with only 43 overs possible, India lost seven wickets for 172 runs but still reached a comfortable 460-9, thanks largely to a fluent 51 (68b, 4x4, 1x6) from Dhruv Jurel. It was the wicketkeeper-batter’s second Test half-century and his first in eight innings. The centrepiece of India’s innings, though, was Devdutt Padikkal’s elegant 167 (230b, 15x4, 1x6), the fourth-highest Test score by an Indian batter in Sri Lanka. Jurel, who came in as a wicketkeeper-batter but is playing as a specialist batter, has for now justified the team management’s decision to pick him ahead of injury replacement Sarfaraz Khan.Ideally, India would like to declare overnight and unleash their pacers in search of early wickets on Day Three, especially after considerable time has already been lost to bad weather, which is expected to affect the remainder of the Test.Play began only at 2.35pm after showers, but Sri Lanka bounced back superbly with the new ball after an ordinary opening day. They took three wickets for 76 runs in 21 overs before tea, with India at 364-5 after resuming at 288-2. The hosts then claimed four more wickets in the final session, conceding 96 runs in 23 overs. Bowling slightly quicker through the air after being too slow on the opening day, the Sri Lankan spinners finally extracted more from the slow surface and reaped the rewards after having bowled 78 overs without much success.Resuming on 131, Padikkal completed his maiden Test 150 off 215 balls with a superb lofted flick over mid-wicket off pacer Asitha Fernando. His long vigil ended when he was stumped off a beauty from Jayasuriya, who held his length back after seeing the left-hander charge down the track.India’s day began on a wrong note when Rishabh Pant (39, 62b, 4x4, 1x6) stepped out and miscued a flighted delivery from Nuwantha to deepish mid-off, where Sonal Dinusha took the catch. It was Nuwantha’s maiden Test wicket. Rahul, who had retired hurt on 77 with cramps on Saturday, resumed after Pant’s dismissal but added only five runs before falling to Nuwantha. He flicked a turning delivery off the back foot to Nishan Fernando at short leg, who took a sharp reflex catch.After tea, Ravindra Jadeja fell lbw for 13 (25b, 1x4) to Nuwantha, unsuccessfully reviewing the decision.Brief scores:India (o/n 288/2) 460/9 in 116 overs (KL Rahul 82, D Padikkal 167, D Jurel 51; Nuwantha 3/175, Jayasuriya 4/109) vs Sri Lanka. Match to continue.
Article Summary: Sri Lanka's spinners finally showed up in the first Test against India. India lost seven wickets for 172 runs but still reached a comfortable 460-9. Devdutt Padikkal’s elegant 167 (230b, 15x4, 1x6) was the fourth-highest Test score by an Indian batter in Sri Lanka.

Article Title: Harmanpreet brace powers India to 3-1 win over Wales in World Cup opener
Article Text:
Harmanpreet Singh scores twice as India beat Wales 3-1 (Agency Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The build-up to India’s FIH World Cup campaign had been clouded by controversies and underwhelming performances in the FIH Pro League. But at the Wagener Hockey Stadium in Amstelveen, Harmanpreet Singh and his men showed they were ready to look ahead.The Indian men’s hockey team celebrated Independence Day with a convincing 3-1 victory over Wales in their campaign opener on Saturday. Sanjay and Harmanpreet, with a brace, put their names on the scoresheet. It was a clinical performance, with India remaining calm under pressure and largely precise with their penalty-corner conversions.All three goals came from penalty corners, with India earning five of them on the day.It was somewhat odd to see the usual Men in Blue turn up in saffron, but much like the bright colour, the Indian team lit up the blue turf with a performance that will give them plenty of confidence. There were lessons too, particularly the need to convert their circle penetrations into field goals.Wales began with a bang, with Jack Pritchard forcing a save from goalkeeper Suraj Karkera in the third minute. India did not have to wait long for their first penalty corner.With their top drag-flicker Harmanpreet off the field, Sanjay stepped up and slotted home in the eighth minute, finding the gap to the right of goalkeeper Toby Reynolds-Cotterill.Harmanpreet doubled India’s advantage in the 11th minute, using deception on his drag-flick to beat Reynolds-Cotterill.India had a scare when Shilanand Lakra took a blow to his upper lip that required sutures, but the striker returned to the field. As India continued to mount pressure, Wales tried to hit on the counter but struggled to create clear opportunities. India went into the break with a 2-0 lead and continued to build on it after the change of ends.Harmanpreet completed his brace in the 43rd minute with a powerful flick, putting India firmly in control.Wales eventually breached India’s defence when Sam Welsh scored in a goalmouth melee, with Mohith scrambling to keep the ball away.Result: India 3 (Sanjay 8, Harmanpreet Singh 11, 43) bt Wales (Sam Welsh 54)
Article Summary: India beat Wales 3-1 in their FIH World Cup opener on Saturday. Sanjay and Harmanpreet Singh both scored twice for the Men in Blue. All three goals came from penalty corners, with India earning five of them on the day.

Article Title: Kush Maini eyes F1 dream as Indian driver targets strong finish to F2 season
Article Text:
Kush Maini (Image via Getty)

London: It’s been a long and bumpy ride for Kush Maini. Seven years after stepping into the world of single-seater racing, the Indian Formula 2 driver is still chasing the destination he has wanted all along: Formula 1.With five rounds remaining in F2, the ART Grand Prix driver is sixth in the standings (88 points) and feels his season has offered plenty of encouragement. Having helped ART turn around a difficult season, Maini believes he has shown enough to be ready for F1, but admits he must stand out in the final five races.“For me, F2 is going very well. I’ve definitely shown the speed. Obviously, the results probably have not been as good as the pace. With five races to go, a lot can happen. F1 is my dream. For me, it’s still very much there and that’s what I’m pushing for. I feel like I’m good enough for F1, 100%, but obviously there’re many drivers who are at this level very good and deserve a chance as well. So I’ve got to stand out in these last five races and then hopefully one day I’ll be able to achieve my dream,” said Maini, who is currently the reserve driver for Mahindra Racing at the Formula E season finale here.
Article Summary: Kush Maini believes he has shown enough to be ready for F1. Indian Formula 2 driver admits he must stand out in the final five races. Maini is currently the reserve driver for Mahindra Racing at the Formula E season finale.

Article Title: China’s long wait, PV Sindhu’s shadow: Chen Yufei, Wang Zhi Yi eye elusive Worlds gold
Article Text:
Wang Zhi Yi

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: China has waited 15 years for a women’s singles World Championships gold, and in Delhi, its hopes once again rest on two formidable names, Chen Yufei and Wang Zhi Yi. Since Wang Yihan’s triumph in 2011, the title has remained beyond Chinese reach, across 10 editions. Yet the drought carries an Indian undertone – P V Sindhu. Chinese contenders have often found her standing between them and glory.Chen, the Tokyo Olympic champion and No. 4 seed, and Wang, the No. 3 seed, have repeatedly crossed Sindhu’s path. Chen leads their career rivalry 9-7; Wang holds a 4-3 edge. Yet, the Indian – seeded ninth – remains a dangerous presence, having beaten Wang at the last Worlds and carrying the aura of a big-stage specialist. At the 2025 Worlds in Paris, Wang was eliminated in the round-of-16 by Sindhu, defeating her 21-17, 21-15 in straight games.“I think I had too much on my mind before playing against Sindhu," Wang said on Saturday. She and former champion Sindhu (2019) could potentially face-off in the pre-quarterfinals. “But I think she is a good player; she just won the Japan Open title, and I think she has been playing better and better, so it’s going to be tough, but I just focus on my first match.”Her immediate opponent is Beiwen Zhang. “I don’t want to think about the result or any title; I just want to focus on the process. ”For Chen, the challenge is equally internal. “The biggest obstacle is myself. If I can conquer myself, then everything will be fine,” she said. A two-time World Championships runner-up and three-time bronze medallist, Chen has the Olympic crown but still craves the Worlds title. “You must have faith and don’t care about anything else. It is just enough,” she said.Asked about whether there's a pressure on Chinese players to win the women's singles title, Chen added: "There is no such pressure. It's just that I just have to do well. I think I will do my best in every match and try to win. It is about ourselves, how we prepare for the event, not for some specific players."Conditions at the refurbished Indira Gandhi (IG) indoor stadium will add another layer. After Saturday’s training, Wang said, “I feel like there was a little bit of wind on the court, so we need to get used to the conditions.” Chen was more reassuring: “The conditions are quite good compared to the last time we played here,” though she admitted, “the weather is not comfortable.”Both, however, appeared satisfied after their opening sessions. But the real test will come when the championships begin on Monday. The Worlds is returning to Indian shores after a gap of 17 years, with the best players looking forward to getting their hands on the coveted title. This time, the Badminton Association of India (BA) has taken some extra steps, learning from the lessons learnt during the controversy-marred India Open in Jan, and even made a sanitary pad machine available for women players, female support staff and officials and spectators.
Article Summary: China has waited 15 years for a women's singles World Championships gold. Since Wang Yihan’s triumph in 2011, the title has remained beyond Chinese reach. The drought carries an Indian undertone – P V Sindhu. Chen leads their career rivalry 9-7; Wang holds a 4-3 edge.

Article Title: ‘We never give up’: Salima Tete confident India can challenge China at World Cup
Article Text:
Indian women’s hockey captain Salima Tete

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Indian women’s hockey captain Salima Tete, the message ahead of their World Cup opener against China is simple — stay confident, stick to the plan and fight until the final whistle.India begin their campaign on Sunday against World No. 4 China in Pool D at Wagener Hockey Stadium in Amstelveen, the Netherlands, knowing that a positive start could set the tone for what they hope will be a successful tournament.And while the team has spent considerable time working on its tactical game, Tete believes the focus has also been on preparing the players to handle the pressure that comes with playing on the biggest stage.“We have mainly worked on our fitness, tactical understanding and our team coordination. We have also focused a lot on improving our decision-making under pressure and being consistent throughout the match,” Tete told TOI.The captain also believes the team has learnt an important lesson from its recent experiences.“The biggest lesson is that we can compete against any strong team if we stay confident and stick to our plans.We have learned that small mistakes can make a big difference at this level, so we need to stay focused and disciplined for the full 60 minutes,” she said.That responsibility will be even greater for Tete, who will lead India into her first World Cup as captain. For the 24-year-old, it is a moment she has dreamt of, but one she also knows comes with added responsibility.“It is a very special and proud moment for me. Playing in a World Cup is a dream for every player, and leading my country as captain makes it even more special,” she said.Tete’s role, however, will extend beyond what she does on the field. She wants to ensure that the team stays united when the pressure begins to mount. “My biggest responsibility will be to lead by example, keep the team motivated and make sure that everyone stays together, especially during difficult moments,” she said.That togetherness, according to Tete, is also one of India’s biggest strengths.“I would say our biggest strength is our fighting spirit and togetherness. We never give up, and we always try to support each other. Even when things don’t go our way, we stay together and keep fighting until the final whistle,” she said.Since Sjoerd Marijne took over as head coach, India have also placed greater emphasis on structure and tactical discipline. Tete feels that work is beginning to reflect in the team’s performances.“We are becoming more confident in our style of play and are learning to adapt to different situations. I think the team is improving with every match,” she said.The first test of that progress will come against China, a side India know will demand their full attention from the opening whistle. “China are a strong team, so we need to start with confidence, stay focused on our plan and play with a lot of energy,” Tete said.For a young Indian side carrying plenty of new faces but also boasting significant experience, that balance between belief and discipline could prove crucial. And for Tete, the challenge is clear: lead from the front, keep the team together and make sure India stay in the fight for all 60 minutes.
Article Summary: India begin their World Cup campaign on Sunday against World No. 4 China. Captain Salima Tete believes the team has learnt an important lesson from its recent experiences. The 24-year-old will lead India into her first World Cup as captain.

Article Title: State associations urge sports ministry to ensure early EFI elections
Article Text:
Union Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya felicitates Mirabai Chanu Saikhom (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: The Indian States Equestrian Association (IESA) on Saturday urged the ministry of youth affairs and sports (MYAS) and the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) to take urgent steps to conduct the long-pending elections to the executive committee of the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI).At a hybrid meeting attended by representatives of equestrian associations from 25 states and Union Territories, the IESA recalled that it had suggested before the Delhi High Court that the IOA appoint an ad hoc committee and complete the election process within three months.“Sadly, despite the lapse of three months since the ad hoc committee was appointed on March 27, 2026, there are no signs of elections being held to the executive committee of the EFI,” Rajasthan Equestrian Association president Raghavendra Singh Dundlod said.The state associations also urged the IOA to include equestrian sport in the National Games schedule and the sports ministry to make the discipline an integral part of the Khelo India Youth Games, citing its growing popularity and India’s performances at international competitions.“The meeting took into account the fact that India has won 14 medals in the Asian Games and five in the Asian Equestrian Championships,” Dundlod said.He added that several state governments reward athletes and offer appointments only to those who have represented their respective states.The IESA also called upon the IOA-appointed ad hoc committee to make public records of all meetings held by it and its sub-committees.“There have been many policy decisions, including selection criteria, event allocation and hike in fees, that the ad hoc committee has made without securing approval of the EFI general body,” Dundlod said.The state associations were also apprised of their responsibilities under the National Sports Governance Act 2025 and the National Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules 2026. They agreed to take necessary remedial measures at the earliest to ensure eligibility for registration with the National Sports Board once the body becomes functional.
Article Summary: The Indian States Equestrian Association (IESA) on Saturday urged the ministry of youth affairs and sports (MYAS) and the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) to take urgent steps to conduct the long-pending elections. The IESA recalled that it had suggested before the Delhi High Court that the IOA appoint an ad hoc committee and complete the election process within three months.

Article Title: Jamshedpur FC seal final quarter-final berth on last day of Durand Cup group stage
Article Text:
Lawmsangzuala after scoring during the Durand Cup. (Pic Credit: Durand Cup Media)

Quarterfinal line-up:

KOLKATA: The last of group stage matches – that were played across three different venues in the east – lived up to its billing as Jamshedpur FC produced a last-day 6-0 rout to make the quarters, Shillong Lajong and Langsning FC enthralled the crowd with a gripping 3-3 draw while Bodoland FC, who were already out of contention for the knockouts, bowed out with a dominating 6-0 thrashing of their local rivals Karbi Anglong Morning Star FC.The star of the day was a teenager playing his first senior tournament for Jamshedpur FC at the 135th Durand Cup – 17-year-old Lawmsangzuala, nicknamed ‘Mama’. The Jamshedpur FC Academy product, who had made his way through the club ranks, came on as a substitute at Birsa Munda Football Stadium in Ranchi and scored a memorable hat-trick that made the Red Miners the last team to qualify for the quarterfinals.They did have to wait for the result of the Shillong derby in an evening fixture at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium where a win for Langsning could have helped them qualify ahead of rivals Lajong and end Jamshedpur’s hopes of progress.However, despite a frantic effort of their attackers, who had already ensured a late comeback draw, for a last-ditch winner was put paid to by the Shillong Lajong defenders.The draw meant that Lajong had qualified from Group E as toppers while Jamshedpur made their way – behind Group C leaders SC Delhi – as the second second-placed qualifiers after East Bengal.Earlier, at Indira Gandhi Athletic Stadium in Guwahati, skipper Holicharan Narzary led Bodoland FC from the front with four goals in their last game, an inconsequential fixture in Group F with NorthEast United FC having already qualified on top.
Article Summary: Lawmsangzuala scored a hat-trick in Jamshedpur FC's last-day 6-0 rout. Shillong Lajong and Langsning FC enthralled the crowd with a gripping 3-3 draw. Bodoland FC, who were already out of contention for the knockouts, bowed out with a dominating6-0 thrashing of local rivals Karbi Anglong Morning Star FC.

Article Title: Subroto Cup to kick off on August 18; 107 teams to compete across three age categories
Article Text:
Air Marshal S. Sivakumar during the official announcement event for 65th Subroto Cup. (PTI Photo)

NEW DELHI: The 65th edition of the prestigious Subroto Cup International Football Tournament will kick off on August 18, with 107 teams set to compete across three age categories in New Delhi NCR and Bengaluru.The tournament, organised by the Subroto Mukerjee Sports Education Society (SMSES) under the aegis of the Air Force Sports Control Board, will be held until Sept 24. The competition will feature Junior Girls (U-17), Sub-Junior Boys (U-15) and Junior Boys (U-17), with more than 215 matches scheduled across the three categories.The official announcement was made on Wednesday in the presence of Air Marshal S. Sivakumar VSM, Air Officer-in-Charge Administration and Vice Chairman of SMSES, who attended as the chief guest. Former India footballer Ashalata Devi Loitongbam was also present as the guest of honour.“The Indian Air Force and SMSES are committed to making the tournament bigger and better every year, providing a platform for young athletes to take the next step in their careers,” Sivakumar said.The Junior Girls (U-17) competition will open the tournament in New Delhi, NCR, from Aug 18 to 27. The Sub-Junior Boys (U-15) category will be held in Bengaluru from Sept 1 to 9, before the Junior Boys (U-17) competition concludes the tournament in New Delhi NCR from Sept 15 to 24.Teams representing various states, Union Territories and educational bodies will participate, with Sri Lanka providing international representation. An age-determination test will also be conducted for the Sub-Junior Boys category in Bengaluru to ensure a level playing field.The matches will be played at venues including Ambedkar Stadium, Tejas Football Ground, Subroto Park Football Ground, Pinto Park Football Ground and Rajokri Football Ground in the Delhi-NCR region. Minerva Public School (CISCE) is the reigning Sub-Junior Boys champion.First held in 1960, the Subroto Cup was conceived by Air Marshal Subroto Mukerjee to promote grassroots football across India.
Article Summary: The 65th edition of the prestigious Subroto Cup International Football Tournament will kick off on August 18. 107 teams will compete across three age categories in New Delhi NCR and Bengaluru. Article Title: Kuldeep, Jadeja, Suthar: Will India play three left-arm spinners in Galle? Coach drops hint

India could field three left-arm spinners in the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle, with bowling coach Morne Morkel saying Kuldeep Yadav Ravindra Jadeja and Manav Suthar offer different skills and can form an attacking bowling combination.Kuldeep brings left-arm wrist spin and an attacking option, Jadeja relies on accuracy, while Suthar bowls a more traditional left-arm spin.“Kuldeep is there, and he's the attacking sort of bowler and for us, his experience and class can't look past. So yeah, I think for us they're all different in their way,” Morkel told the media here on Thursday.“So one (Suthar) turns a bit more, one (Jadeja) is slightly more accurate and I don't think it's a (three left-arm spinners) massive concern for us.“It’s just how Gill is going to use those guys at certain times. Article Title: How India’s WTC final hopes take a hit after Bangladesh's historic win over Australia: Explained

Bangladesh pulled off a nine-wicket win over Australia in Darwin on Sunday, giving them one of the biggest wins in Test cricket and leaving Australia's 20-Test schedule over the next 12 months off to a difficult start.Cameron Green's maiden Test century at home delayed the result, but Bangladesh had already taken control of the match after three-and-a-half days of cricket on a Marrara Stadium pitch that offered a good contest between bat and ball.The result was unexpected given the records of the two teams. Australia had reached the last two World Test Championship (WTC) finals and won 18 of their previous 23 Tests. Bangladesh, meanwhile, had lost 22 of their previous 26 Tests outside Asia and had suffered innings defeats against Zimbabwe and a Cricket Australia XI in the previous two months.Yet Najmul Hossain Shanto's side produced a nine-wicket win in their first Test in Australia since 2003. It was Bangladesh's first long-format tour of Australia in 23 years and one of the biggest results in the country's 40-year history in international cricket.The result has also changed the WTC picture.Before the Darwin Test, Bangladesh were fourth in the WTC standings, one place above India. However, they had played only four Tests at that stage — losing 0-1 to Sri Lanka and beating Pakistan 2-0 at home — so their position was largely viewed in the context of the small number of matches they had played.Their win in Darwin has now pushed Bangladesh to 66.67 per cent, while India remain on 48.15 per cent.India had entered the Sri Lanka series after drawing 2-2 in England and beating the West Indies 2-0 at home. Their progress was then checked by a 0-2 home series defeat to South Africa.The two Tests in Sri Lanka were expected to be an important part of India's push for a place in next year's WTC final. But rain disrupted the second day of the opening Test in Galle after India had made a strong start, while more rain is forecast over the next three days.Bangladesh's win in Darwin has widened the gap between them and India to more than 18 percentage points.For India, the remaining WTC schedule leaves little room for dropped points. After Sri Lanka, they travel to New Zealand for two Tests before hosting Australia in a five-Test series.New Zealand have proved difficult opponents for India in their own conditions, while India may need something close to a 4-0 series win against Australia to remain in contention for the WTC final.

Article Title: Dhruv Jurel breaks seven-innings fifty drought, says 'there was honestly no pressure'

Article Title: Manchester Super Giants, Trent Rockets crowned champions as The Hundred 2026 ends in Lord’s glory
Article Text:
The Hundred 2026 winners (Image: X)

Seifert powers Manchester to maiden title

Trent Rockets Women complete a one-sided triumph

Manchester Super Giants clinched their maiden men’s title while Trent Rockets Women lifted their first-ever trophy as The Hundred’s sixth season reached a dramatic conclusion at Lord’s. The Hundred’s sixth season signed off in style at Lord’s, with Manchester Super Giants and Trent Rockets sharing the spotlight on a Finals Day that produced two contrasting title deciders.Manchester Super Giants, formerly known as Manchester Originals, survived a late collapse to defeat Trent Rockets by five wickets in the men’s final, while Trent Rockets Women produced a ruthless display to crush Sunrisers Leeds by eight wickets and claim their maiden title.The Trent Rockets also walked away with an additional prize, winning the inaugural Helix trophy for the best combined franchise performance across the men’s and women’s competitions.The men’s final looked to be slipping away from Manchester Super Giants before Tim Seifert intervened with a breathtaking assault. Trent Rockets posted 158 for 8 from their 100 balls, with Aneurin Donald leading the recovery with a rapid 38 off 19 balls, while captain Lewis Gregory contributed 32 from 19.The Rockets had made a steady start through Ben Duckett, but their momentum was checked by a double blow. Spinner Noor Ahmad was involved in the dismissal of captain Sam Billings before removing Tim David for a duck, leaving Manchester with an opening to seize control.Donald and Gregory then rebuilt the innings with aggressive strokeplay, pushing Trent towards a competitive total of 158. Manchester's response began with a clear intent to attack.Seifert turned the chase into a spectacle, smashing 72 off just 38 balls, including seven sixes. His calculated aggression kept Manchester ahead of the required rate and put the Rockets under immense pressure. Paul Walter provided valuable support, adding 22 off 14 balls, with the pair putting together a blistering 66-run stand from only 31 balls.But just when Manchester appeared certain to cruise home, the final overs produced a dramatic twist. Mohammad Amir dragged the Super Giants back into the contest with a superb spell, conceding just 29 runs and helping create six consecutive dot balls. Heinrich Klaasen and Michael Bracewell also departed as the pressure suddenly mounted.With Manchester needing a boundary to settle the nerves, Liam Dawson delivered. He launched a towering six over deep midwicket with just two balls remaining, taking Manchester Super Giants to 162 for 5 after 98 balls and sealing their first men's title.Noor Ahmad finished with three wickets for Manchester, while Amir claimed three for Trent Rockets, but it was Seifert's extraordinary innings that ultimately defined the final.If the men's final went down to the wire, the women's contest was almost the complete opposite. Trent Rockets Women dismantled Sunrisers Leeds, formerly Northern Superchargers, to secure a commanding eight-wicket victory and their first Hundred women's title.Sunrisers Leeds never found their footing after being reduced to 26 for 3 during the 25-ball powerplay. The collapse continued through the middle overs as Trent's bowlers squeezed the life out of the defending champions' batting line-up.Annabel Sutherland top-scored with 25 from 23 balls, while Dani Gibson made 22 off 16. Phoebe Litchfield was dismissed for just 10, and Sutherland's dismissal further exposed a fragile middle order. Georgia Adams and Charley Phillips were particularly effective, taking two wickets apiece for just nine and 12 runs respectively.Sunrisers Leeds were eventually bowled out for only 91 in 91 balls, leaving Trent Rockets with a straightforward target. They wasted little time.Sophia Dunkley immediately attacked the bowling, smashing 41 from 23 balls, while Beth Mooney provided the composure to finish the job unbeaten on 31 from 21 deliveries. Trent Rockets reached 92 for 2 in only 54 balls, leaving 46 deliveries unused and completing a dominant eight-wicket victory.
Article Summary: Manchester Super Giants beat Trent Rockets by five wickets in men's final. Trent Rockets Women crush Sunrisers Leeds by eight wickets to win women's title. Tim Seifert's 72 powers Manchester to maiden title at Lord's.

Article Title: ‘Going to go back to bed now’: Devdutt Padikkal after career-best 167 in Galle Test
Article Text:
Devdutt Padikkal

How Padikkal Took on Sri Lanka’s Spinners

The Hunger to Keep Scoring

Devdutt Padikkal said his maiden Test century against Sri Lanka was the result of two years of hard work and preparation, after the left-hander scored a career-best 167 in the first Test at Galle.Resuming from an overnight score of 131, Padikkal batted for 230 balls and hit 15 fours and a six to help India reach 460/9 on a rain-hit second day. The Karnataka batter said he had long prepared himself to make the most of an opportunity at the international level.“Definitely. I've dreamt of this moment. For the last two years, I've been working really hard to try and make sure that when I get that opportunity, I can do something special like this, and I'm really happy to do that," Padikkal said.Padikkal played with positive intent against spin, using confident footwork and attacking shots to put pressure back on the bowlers."I think we have discussed that at length, especially when you're playing spin, it's important that you have certain plans in your head.“You cannot go out there and expect to react all the time. It's important that we have a couple of shots in your head that you want to play as soon as you go out there, so that you can put some pressure on the bowler as well.So, I think over the last year or so, we have really worked on trying to find ways in our own strengths that you can really implement to make sure that you put pressure back."He said clarity and complete commitment to every shot had improved his footwork and confidence.Padikkal did not stop after reaching his century and converted it into 167. He said staying focused immediately after reaching a milestone was crucial."I think honestly, it's just the hunger to score more runs. I just enjoy batting out there, and the moment you get to 100, it's easy to relax and feel that relief. But it's important that for me, the next 20-30 balls are the really important phase that I try and make sure that I'm completely focused, completely there.“I think when I get past those first 10 balls after 100, I think it makes my job a whole lot easier and over the years, I've seen so many cricketers get big runs, get big hundreds, especially back in Karnataka. So just watching them bat makes me want to do the same."Padikkal expects the Galle pitch to become more challenging over the next few days. After his long innings in humid conditions, however, his celebration plans were simple: "Not really. I think I'm tired, so I'm just going to go back to bed now," he concluded.
Article Summary: Devdutt Padikkal scored a career-best 167 in the first Test at Galle. He batted for 230 balls and hit 15 fours and a six to help India reach 460/9. The Karnataka batter said he had long prepared himself to make the most of an opportunity.

Article Title: 'We weren’t looking to go bonkers': Dhruv Jurel reveals India’s strategy after 460/9 on Day 2

India wicketkeeper-batter Dhruv Jurel revealed that the visitors had a clear plan to score quickly but sensibly on the rain-affected second day of the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle. India eventually ended the day at 460/9, with Kuldeep Yadav unbeaten on 12 and Prasidh Krishna on 1.Jurel walked in after India had already lost KL Rahul and Rishabh Pant but played an attacking knock to keep the momentum going. The right-hander struck 51 off 68 deliveries, including four fours and a six. He added a crucial 55-run partnership with Manav Suthar, helping India cross the 400-run mark.“There was a plan to score runs briskly, but sensibly. We weren’t looking to go bonkers from ball one, but there was a plan,” Jurel said during the post-match press conference.The India batter also revealed that his previous experience of playing in Sri Lanka with India A helped him understand the conditions and approach the innings with confidence.“I know conditions here, having played for India A here. I was under no pressure, it’s a privilege to play for India,” Jurel added.Jurel was given a reprieve on 29 when Sri Lankan captain Dhananjaya de Silva dropped a difficult chance at first slip.However, the captain later made amends by taking a spectacular catch to dismiss Jurel off Prabath Jayasuriya.The standout performer for India was Devdutt Padikkal, who continued his sensational form from Day 1 to score a magnificent 167 off 230 balls. Padikkal's innings included 15 fours and a six, and he became only the third Indian batter to score 150 or more against Sri Lanka from the No. 3 position, joining Rahul Dravid and Cheteshwar Pujara.Jurel was full of praise for his teammate and pointed out that Padikkal has consistently delivered whenever opportunities have come his way.“Devdutt scores whenever he gets a chance,” Dhruv Jurel said.Padikkal's dismissal eventually triggered another phase of Sri Lankan pressure, with Prabath Jayasuriya finishing with 4/109 and Keshara Nuwantha taking 3/175.Despite India's imposing total, Jurel knows the job is far from finished. The wicketkeeper-batter stressed that India's bowlers will need to maintain discipline and be prepared for long spells when Sri Lanka begin their first innings.“We need to bowl long spells here and be consistent with lengths. India began the day at 288/2 and lost seven wickets for 172 runs, but still managed to build a formidable first-innings total. Despite losing seven wickets for 172 runs during a truncated day, India retained a commanding position after Sri Lanka's bowlers fought back strongly in the final two sessions.Heavy rain and a wet outfield washed out the entire morning session, with play finally resuming at 2:35 PM local time. India had begun the day at a dominant 288/2 and managed to add 172 runs before stumps, but Sri Lanka's improved bowling effort prevented the visitors from running away with the game.Kuldeep Yadav (12)* and Prasidh Krishna (1)* were at the crease when play was called off.Resuming on an unbeaten 131, Padikkal continued his impressive performance at No. 3 and completed his maiden 150-plus Test score. The left-hander eventually made 167 off 230 balls, hitting 15 fours and a six. He became only the third Indian batter to score 150 or more against Sri Lanka from No. 3, joining Rahul Dravid (177) and Cheteshwar Pujara (153).Padikkal's innings finally ended when Prabath Jayasuriya deceived him in flight. Rishabh Pant was the first to go, falling for 39 off 62 balls. Article Title: 'We weren’t able to catch': Steve Smith admits Australia were 'outplayed' after historic Bangladesh defeat
Article Text:
Steve Smith (Image: ANI)

‘We’re the number one team for a reason’

How Bangladesh scripted history in Darwin

Bangladesh produced a historic performance in Darwin, defeating Australia by nine wickets in the first Test to secure their first-ever Test victory on Australian soil. The defeat brought Australia’s long run of consistency under scrutiny, but Steve Smith was quick to acknowledge Bangladesh’s superior performance while insisting that one poor Test does not change Australia’s status as the world’s top-ranked Test side.“Pretty simple: we were outplayed. I thought Bangladesh bowled really well the first morning, really disciplined. Our batters probably weren’t disciplined enough,” Smith said after the defeat, as quoted by The Daily Star.Australia struggled with the bat across both innings. After being bowled out for 198 in their first innings, they were forced to concede a massive 228-run lead after Bangladesh piled up 426. Smith, who scored 71 in the first innings, admitted that Australia failed to capitalise when their batters got starts.“They got too many in front, and we weren’t able to catch it up yesterday on what was a pretty decent wicket to bat on. A couple of us got starts and didn’t go on with it. Greeny, I thought, played really nicely to get a hundred, but he didn’t have any partners to go with him,” he said. Cameron Green provided Australia with some resistance in the second innings, scoring a fighting 104, but the hosts were eventually dismissed for 284. Bangladesh were left with only 57 runs to chase for victory.Despite the heavy defeat, Smith backed Australia to bounce back and urged the team not to overreact to what he described as a poor week.“I hope it’s one bad week. We’re the number one team for a reason. We’ve played really good, consistent cricket over a long period of time, and this week was a bit of a blip,” Smith said.The experienced batter also gave full credit to Bangladesh for their performance throughout the four-day contest.“We could have done things a lot better, but credit goes to them for the way they played throughout these last four days,” he added.Australia were bowled out for 198 after Hasan Mahmud ’s stunning 6/55, before Bangladesh piled on 426, led by centuries from Tanzid Hasan and strong knocks from Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mehidy Hasan Miraz. Josh Hazlewood took six wickets and reached 300 Test wickets.Cameron Green’s 104 helped Australia fight back in the second innings, but Mehidy Hasan Miraz’s 5/66 and Hasan Mahmud’s three wickets restricted them to 284.Chasing 57, Bangladesh reached the target in just 14.2 overs, winning by nine wickets to secure their first-ever Test victory on Australian soil. Hasan Mahmud was named Player of the Match.

Devdutt Padikkal's sensational innings came to an end in the opening Test against Sri Lanka as the India batter was dismissed for a magnificent 167 off 230 balls in Galle. Padikkal, who had struck his maiden Test century on Day 1, continued his remarkable run on the rain-affected second day and went on to register his first Test score beyond 150.The left-hander smashed 15 fours and a six during his memorable knock, anchoring India's innings and keeping the visitors in a commanding position despite repeated interruptions caused by rain.With his 150-plus score, Padikkal became only the third Indian batter to score 150 or more against Sri Lanka from No. 3. The 24-year-old received a standing ovation from the Galle crowd as he walked back to the pavilion, while his India teammates also stood up to applaud his superb effort.Padikkal was handed the No. 3 role following Sudharsan's injury and responded with a career-defining performance. His maiden century also made him the first Indian batter to score a Test century on Independence Day, while he became only the second Indian cricketer after Virat Kohli to score an international century on August 15.Once play finally resumed, India suffered two quick setbacks. Rishabh Pant was dismissed for 39 off 62 balls, caught by Sonal Dinusha at short mid-off while attempting to play Keshara Nuwantha.KL Rahul, who had retired hurt with cramps on Day 1, returned to the crease but could not convert his impressive start into a century. He was dismissed for 82 off 175 balls, with Nishan Fernando taking a sharp catch at short leg off Nuwantha.
Article Summary: Devdutt Padikkal dismissed for 167 off 230 balls in Galle. Left-hander smashed 15 fours and a six during his memorable knock. He became only the third Indian batter to score 150 or more against Sri Lanka from No. 3. Rishabh Pant was dismissed for 39 off 62 balls.

Article Title: ‘Clearly, there’s something wrong’: Sunil Gavaskar questions India’s fitness methods amid injury crisis
Article Text:
Sunil Gavaskar. (BCCI Photo)

Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar has questioned India's approach to player fitness after a series of injuries left several key players on the sidelines, while defending the physios at the BCCI 's Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru.Jasprit Bumrah, Sai Sudharsan, Washington Sundar, Hardik Pandya, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Harshit Rana are among the Indian players currently unavailable due to injuries. The growing list has triggered questions over injury management, with scrutiny directed towards head coach Gautam Gambhir , chairman of selectors Ajit Agarkar and the CoE.However, Gavaskar believes it is unfair to place the responsibility on the physios at the Bengaluru facility. The 1983 World Cup winner pointed out that hamstring injuries have been particularly common among Indian players and argued that their training methods need closer examination.VVS Laxman , the Head of Cricket, recently explained the functioning of the CoE alongside BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia and defended the facility's physios, stressing that the centre is not simply a "rehab centre". Gavaskar has now echoed that view."While Bumrah has a knee injury, it is seen that most Indian players suffer from hamstring injuries. Clearly, there’s something wrong with their training, and that’s why these recurring hamstring injuries. These injuries happen when they are playing for India, but unfortunately, the blame is put on the physios at the BCCI centre of excellence," wrote Gavaskar in his column for Mid-Day.Gavaskar also questioned the increasingly common restrictions placed on bowlers during net sessions under the idea of managing their biomechanics and workloads."The so-called biomechanics, where a bowler can bowl only so many deliveries in the practice nets, is a questionable practice. Even in the IPL, it is learnt that some of the overseas physios don’t allow the bowlers to bowl more than 20 balls in the nets. If in the match you will be bowling 24 balls, that is, if you don’t bowl no-balls and wides, then how is bowling a lesser number in the nets going to help?" he added.The former India captain also challenged the emphasis placed on gym-based fitness, suggesting that players should focus more on being prepared for the demands of actual matches.Gavaskar believes the recurring injuries require a detailed assessment rather than simply attributing them to the medical staff at the CoE."It’s an issue that needs a good, hard look at why these injuries are happening again and again. It is more important to be match fit than gym fit. But then, maybe I am from a generation that had different ideas on fitness," wrote Gavaskar.India's injury concerns have also been highlighted by captain Shubman Gill . Following the ODI series defeat against England, Gill expressed frustration at the constant changes to the playing XI because of injuries.Gill pointed towards the demands of the upcoming World Cup, where India could have to play nine to 10 matches, and questioned how players would manage that workload if they are currently struggling to remain available for even two or three games.With several players sidelined and recurring hamstring issues becoming a concern, the debate over India's fitness methods and injury management is likely to continue. Gavaskar's comments shift some of the focus away from the CoE physios and towards the broader approach to player training and match readiness.
Article Summary: Sunil Gavaskar questions India's approach to player fitness after series of injuries. Former captain defends physios at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence (CoE) Jasprit Bumrah, Sai Sudharsan, Washington Sundar, Hardik Pandya, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Harshit Rana are among the Indian players currently unavailable due to injuries.

Article Title: ‘Very embarrassing defeat’: Ricky Ponting tears apart Australia after Bangladesh shock
Article Text:
Australian captain Pat Cummins, leads his players from the field following their nine wicket loss to Banglade (Image via AP)

Former Australia captains and batters Ricky Ponting and Matthew Hayden have called for changes to Australia's Test team after Bangladesh inflicted a historic nine-wicket defeat on Pat Cummins ' side in Darwin.Australia were comprehensively outplayed in the opening Test, suffering their first Test defeat to Bangladesh on home soil. The result has prompted calls for the selectors to begin rebuilding the side ahead of the second Test in Mackay, Queensland, starting on August 22.Ponting, speaking to Channel 7, described the loss as a "very embarrassing defeat" and said the result should force Australia to begin regenerating the team."Look, I’m the last one who wants to make change. As a captain or as a player, I wanted to keep the group together," the former Australia captain said.Ponting stressed that he had previously been reluctant to advocate for major changes, but believed there had already been enough signs before the series that Australia could start introducing fresh faces."It has to get to a bad point before I start saying you ought to leave somebody out. But there had been enough evidence for me coming here to suggest that they weren’t going to lose anything or much at all by starting that regeneration, by maybe bringing in another opener, by maybe bringing in someone at No.3," he said."And I think if they lose here, then I think that has to happen."Matthew Hayden also backed the idea of reshaping Australia's batting order, suggesting Sam Konstas and Matt Renshaw should be brought back into the side.Hayden believes Travis Head should move down the order rather than continue opening, while he questioned Alex Carey's position at No. 5."(Opening is) not (Head’s) best position. I think his best position is still at No. 5. I don’t like Alex Carey coming out at No. 5," Hayden said.The former Australia opener said the current combination appeared uncertain despite the depth available in Australian cricket."It just feels a little shaky and uncertain," he added. "And why are we in this position? Australian cricket is so strong. It doesn’t need to be in that position, in my opinion."Hayden also acknowledged that selecting the replacements would not be straightforward, particularly when deciding between players with current match fitness and those with greater potential."But who you pick, that’s a great question. Are you picking match-fit players or are you picking players on talent? Like a Sammy Konstas, for example?" he said.Australia's batting struggles were exposed during the first Test after they were bowled out for 198 in their first innings. Bangladesh responded with 426, taking a 228-run lead.Cameron Green offered Australia's strongest resistance in the second innings with 104, his third Test century and first in Australia. However, Mehidy Hasan Miraz claimed five wickets as Australia were dismissed for 284.Bangladesh then chased a target of 57 in only 14.2 overs, losing one wicket to complete a landmark victory.The result has increased pressure on Australia's selectors, with Ponting and Hayden now joining the growing calls for changes before the second Test.
Article Summary: Former Australia captains Ricky Ponting and Matthew Hayden have called for changes to Australia's Test team. Australia were comprehensively outplayed in the opening Test, suffering their first Test defeat to Bangladesh on home soil. The result has prompted calls for the selectors to begin rebuilding the side ahead of the second Test in Mackay.
